name: A-Mem: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
authors: Wujiang Xu, Zujie Liang, Kai Mei, Hang Gao, Juntao Tan, Yongfeng Zhang (lead affiliation: Rutgers University; also AIOS Foundation)
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems); arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.12110
code_url: https://github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem (benchmark/eval) and https://github.com/WujiangXu/A-mem-sys (memory system); mirror: https://github.com/agiresearch/A-mem
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (LLM-driven, agentic): the LLM autonomously generates structured notes, decides on memory links, and revises/evolves prior memory notes. No learned critic and no external verifier; reflection is over the memory store rather than over task answers.
feedback_source: self-generated. The same LLM analyzes new and historical memories to produce keywords/tags/contextual descriptions, propose links, and trigger evolution of existing notes. No external tool, unit test, environment reward, or ground-truth oracle is used in the memory loop (the LLM judges relevance/links itself).
iteration_structure: iterative-refine over a growing memory network rather than per-task retry: each newly added memory triggers (1) note construction, (2) link generation to nearest neighbors, and (3) memory evolution that can update the context/keywords/tags of existing historical notes. There is no episodic-retry-with-reset or tree/MCTS search of the answer.
reflection_object: prompt/context and structured-notes/graph memory: A-Mem reflects on and modifies the persistent memory representation (structured atomic notes with contextual descriptions, keywords, tags, embeddings, and inter-note links) that is later retrieved into the agent context. It does not modify the reasoning chain, action trajectory of a task, reusable skills/workflows, agent code, or model weights.
requires_training: none. A-Mem is a training-free, inference-time memory system built on frozen foundation models; it only requires LLM API calls plus a fixed sentence-embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2). No SFT/RL/DPO.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge: the underlying LLM itself decides note attributes, which historical notes to link, and whether/how to evolve existing notes. No trained reward model, verifiable reward, or separate retrospective/meta-judge model.
distillation_target: episodic-memory organized as structured-notes/graph. Reflection is distilled into a continually re-organized Zettelkasten-style knowledge network of atomic memory notes (with LLM-generated contextual descriptions, keywords, tags, embeddings, and links), not into reusable skills, a constitution, a single prompt, or model weights.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered: the agentic memory behavior (note construction, link generation, memory evolution) is prompt/scaffold-engineered via designed templates (P_s1 for note generation, P_s3 for evolution) around frozen LLMs. It is not an RL-emergent reflective behavior like the R1 'aha' moment.
memory_type: structured-notes/graph (long-term-episodic). Zettelkasten-inspired interconnected network of atomic memory notes, each storing original content, timestamp, LLM-generated keywords, tags, a contextual description, an embedding vector, and a set of links to related notes.
memory_persistence: cross-session / cross-episode: the memory network persists and accumulates across the full long-term conversation (e.g., LoCoMo up to ~35 sessions / 9K tokens; DialSim ~1,300 sessions over five years / ~350K tokens), continuously refining as new memories arrive.
memory_curation_mechanism: overwrite/evolution (self-relinking): when a new memory is added, the system links it to its nearest-neighbor notes and then evolves those neighbors — the LLM may update their contextual descriptions, keywords, and tags, with the evolved note m_j* replacing the original m_j. Retrieval is also retrieval-gated via top-k (k=10) cosine similarity over embeddings, keeping injected context bounded (~1,200-2,500 tokens).
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level with respect to task answers — A-Mem does not localize errors in a reasoning chain or step. At the memory level, organization is note-level (per atomic memory note) and link-level (pairwise relations between notes), but there is no token/step error attribution.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task / cross-session transfer of experience: the system accumulates and reorganizes historical memories across many sessions and reuses them via retrieval for later queries, rather than refining a single answer within one task.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only / not framed as failure recovery: A-Mem improves future answers by providing better-organized retrieved context; it has no mid-trajectory recovery or post-hoc revision of a wrong answer. There is no explicit failure signal in the loop.
task_domains: QA/reasoning over long-term dialogue (long-term conversational memory): multi-hop, temporal, open-domain, single-hop, and adversarial (unanswerable) question answering grounded in extended multi-session conversations. Positioned generally as memory for LLM agents.
benchmarks: LoCoMo (long-term conversational QA, 7,512 QA pairs across 5 categories: Multi-Hop, Temporal, Open-Domain, Single-Hop, Adversarial; avg ~9K tokens, up to 35 sessions) and DialSim (multi-party TV-show dialogue QA: Friends, The Big Bang Theory, The Office; ~1,300 sessions, ~350K tokens).
headline_result: On LoCoMo with GPT-4o-mini, A-Mem achieves a Multi-Hop ROUGE-L of 44.27, more than doubling the strongest baseline LoCoMo's 18.09 (METEOR 23.43 vs 7.61; SBERT 70.49 vs 52.30). With non-GPT models the gap is larger (Qwen2.5 Multi-Hop ROUGE-L 27.23 vs LoCoMo 4.68 / ReadAgent 2.81, a near six-fold improvement). On DialSim, A-Mem reaches F1 3.45 (+35% over LoCoMo's 2.55 and +192% over MemGPT's 1.18). Evaluated across six foundation models.
baselines: LoCoMo (the dataset's own memory method), ReadAgent, MemoryBank, and MemGPT. Compared under identical system prompts; LoCoMo and MemGPT are the strongest comparators (especially on Open-Domain and Adversarial categories for GPT models).
gains_vs_baseline: Largest gains on complex Multi-Hop reasoning: roughly 2x or more over the best baseline (GPT-4o-mini Multi-Hop ROUGE-L 44.27 vs 18.09; '~at least two times better' on multi-hop), up to ~6x on some non-GPT models. Note GPT-based baselines (LoCoMo, MemGPT) remain competitive or stronger on simpler Open-Domain and Adversarial categories due to strong pre-trained factual recall, so the advantage is task-dependent and concentrated in multi-hop/compositional reasoning.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-time only; markedly cheaper than baselines despite multiple LLM calls for memory processing: ~1,200-2,500 tokens per memory operation vs ~16,900 tokens for LoCoMo/MemGPT (an 85-93% reduction in token usage via selective top-k retrieval), at <$0.0003 per memory operation. Storage is O(N) like other vector stores; retrieval time scales sub-linearly (0.31us to 3.70us when scaling to 1M memories), so no extra storage/retrieval overhead vs baselines.
known_limitations: Authors note: (1) memory-organization quality is bounded by the underlying LLM's capability — different LLMs produce different contextual descriptions and link decisions, so weaker base models yield weaker organization; (2) the implementation is text-only and does not yet handle multimodal information (images/audio). Implicit limits: gains are concentrated on multi-hop reasoning while strong GPT baselines can match or exceed A-Mem on simple open-domain/adversarial factual recall; evaluation is confined to long-term conversational QA (LoCoMo, DialSim).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only / self-verify: the memory-construction, linking, and evolution loop uses no external tool, verifier, ground-truth label, or environment reward — relevance and link decisions are made by the LLM itself. Ground-truth answers are used only for final evaluation metrics, not as feedback inside the memory loop.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent (net-positive on the targeted setting): A-Mem improves long-term conversational QA, with the clearest, large gains on multi-hop/compositional reasoning, but baselines remain competitive or better on simple open-domain/adversarial recall for strong GPT models. There is no label leakage in the memory loop, so improvements come from better retrieval/organization rather than oracle feedback.
calibration_effect: not-measured: the paper does not report calibration / overconfidence effects (no calibration or confidence-accuracy analysis); evaluation is restricted to QA quality metrics (F1, BLEU-1, ROUGE-L/2, METEOR, SBERT) and efficiency.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a — A-Mem is a memory system, not a failure-attribution method; it does not classify failure modes, attribute responsible agents, or localize failing steps.
failure_mode_addressed: Indirectly targets long-context / long-term memory failures: loss of long-range dependencies and cross-session inconsistency in extended conversations, and rigidity of fixed memory operations/structures in prior systems (which it addresses with dynamic linking and memory evolution). Not framed against MAST's multi-agent failure taxonomy.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset released; A-Mem evaluates on existing benchmarks (LoCoMo, DialSim). It releases open-source code: benchmark/eval repo (A-mem) and the agentic memory system (A-mem-sys).
builds_on: Zettelkasten note-taking method (Ahrens, 'How to Take Smart Notes'); prior LLM-agent memory systems used as baselines/predecessors: MemGPT, MemoryBank, ReadAgent, and the LoCoMo memory method; related retrieval/RAG and self-reflection lines (e.g., Self-RAG). Built on frozen foundation models (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5, Llama 3.2, DeepSeek-R1-32B, Claude 3/3.5 Haiku) with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings.
extended_by_or_inspired: As a widely-cited 2025 agentic-memory work (~600 citations), it is referenced across the LLM-agent memory literature and memory-system surveys/benchmarks (e.g., comparisons against Mem0 and other long-term memory frameworks, and memory-evaluation efforts such as LongMemEval-style studies). Specific named successors are not enumerated in the paper itself. [uncertain]
citation_count: 603 (Semantic Scholar, CorpusID:276421617; influential citation count 89). Approximate; rises over time.
reasoning_model_native: Not native to reasoning models, but model-agnostic and tested with a reasoning model: A-Mem is a scaffold around frozen LLMs and includes DeepSeek-R1-32B among its six evaluated foundation models. The reflective/memory behavior is engineered, not an intrinsic property of o1/R1-style built-in reflection.
on_policy_distillation_link: n/a — no policy training or distillation into weights/skills; experience is 'distilled' only into an evolving in-context memory graph, so there is no direct link to on-policy distillation or skill-optimization in the weight-update sense.
sample_efficiency: [uncertain] — not reported as a learning-curve / number-of-trials metric; A-Mem is training-free and accumulates memory online per interaction. Related efficiency reported: top-k retrieval with k=10 and ~1,200-2,500 tokens per memory operation.
